2608.27146.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
2608.27146.paper_summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents must rely on untrusted runtime Observations to complete open-ended tasks; however, when tool outputs no longer merely provide data but begin to specify concrete actions, they effectively become ``commands'' that can drive real-world side effects beyond user intent. We argue that this risk arises from conflating action induction with execution authorization. To address this distinction, we propose SARA, which treats action induction and execution authorization as distinct runtime roles and separates action provenance from execution authority. On the Observation side, a context-isolated Action Probe exposes action-inducing semantics and persistently records action-origin provenance across steps as a review signal; on the execution side, actual tool calls are authorized only against the user objective and audited evidence from authorized successful executions, while satisfying goal, execution-chain, and argument-level support. To preserve this separation across multi-step execution, SARA applies No-History-Promotion to prevent historical recurrence from laundering action origins into execution authority. Across AgentDojo and AgentDyn, SARA limits ASR to no more than \(0.63\%\) across four primary evaluation settings while maintaining competitive task utility, and consistently reduces ASR across additional Agent backbones.
2608.27146.paper_summary_zh: 工具增強的 LLM 代理必須依賴不受信任的運行時觀察來完成開放式任務；然而，當工具的輸出不再僅僅提供數據，而是開始指定具體行動時，它們實際上變成了可以驅動超出用戶意圖的現實世界副作用的「命令」。我們認為，這種風險源於將行動誘導與執行授權混為一談。為了解決這一區別，我們提出了 SARA，它將行動誘導和執行授權視為不同的運行時角色，並將行動來源與執行權限分開。在觀察方面，一個上下文隔離的行動探針揭示了誘導行動的語義，並持續記錄跨步驟的行動來源作為審查信號；在執行方面，實際的工具調用僅根據用戶目標和來自授權成功執行的審計證據進行授權，同時滿足目標、執行鏈和參數級別的支持。為了在多步執行中保持這一分離，SARA 應用無歷史促進以防止歷史重現將行動來源洗白為執行權限。在 AgentDojo 和 AgentDyn 中，SARA 將 ASR 限制在四個主要評估設置中不超過 \(0.63\%\)，同時保持競爭性的任務效用，並在額外的代理骨幹中持續減少 ASR。
